title: Spine X-ray
what: An X-ray picture of your spine. It shows the bones and vertebrae. The radiation dose is small.
why: For back or neck pain after an injury, a curved spine, or to check results after treatment.
tell_doctor: If you are pregnant or not sure
If you recently had an X-ray with contrast dye
If it is hard for you to stand or lie down

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: For the neck and upper back, no special preparation is needed.

prepare.title: Lower back
prepare.text: For a lower back X-ray, you may be asked to avoid foods that cause gas the day before and to empty your bowels. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Take off jewelry, necklaces, your belt, and any bra with metal. Metal shows up on the image.

steps: You undress to the waist or lower, depending on the part of the spine
You stand or lie down by the machine
The technician puts you in the right position and steps out
You need to stay still and hold your breath for a few seconds
Usually two pictures are taken, from the front and the side, sometimes while you bend
feel: Nothing. You cannot feel the X-ray itself
If your back hurts, it may be hard to hold the position. Tell the technician
after: You can go back to your day right away
The images and report are usually ready the same day or the next day
red_flags: If your arms or legs go numb or weak after an injury, do not move on your own. Call emergency services
Back pain with trouble peeing or numbness in the groin: see a doctor right away or call emergency services

faq.a: The dose is small. The doctor orders an X-ray when the benefit is greater than the risk. Tell them in advance if you are pregnant.

faq.q: Can an X-ray show a herniated disc?
faq.a: No. An X-ray shows bones. A herniated disc shows up on an MRI.
